title: Bodycam Released in Crash of UPS Airlines Flight 2976
description:
Bodycam video obtained by Midwest Safety involving the Crash of UPS Airlines Flight 2976. If you are a member of the media requesting access or more info, please email Tips@Midwest-Safety.com

GoFundMe: https://www.gofundme.com/c/act/kentucky-plane-crash-relief

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this.

TIPS: Submit a tip: 
https://midwest.clickup.com/forms/9006119175/p/f/8ccwy87-63537/H3BKH5EZAPIBRYJ1XB/tips

PRIVACY or COMPLAINTS: Privacy concern or other issue:
https://midwest.clickup.com/forms/9006119175/f/8ccwy87-63557/LE0PT31DZVHHEIE5AW

EMAIL US: contact@midwest-safety.com

MERCH: Midwest-Safety.com

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: contact@midwest-safety.com

Investigations ensued, and footage from several other sources were eventually released.
Recent NTSB updates show the MD-11's engine detaching and passing over the wing during takeoff.
Investigators found fatigue cracks and overstress failure in the engine pylon's spherical bearing, which mounts the engine to the aircraft.
Despite its design to handle a lost engine, the damage to the wing and flames potentially entering a second engine were likely causes for a failed takeoff, reaching speeds of 212 miles an hour.
There was likely nothing the crew could do to avoid a crash.
An NTSB report notes the engine pylon is typically inspected every five years.
Reports indicate this aircraft underwent maintenance in San Antonio from September 3 to October 18, 2025, about two weeks prior to the crash.
Investigators are now examining whether the pylons were inspected, whether negligence occurred, and if regulations need updating.
In the latest update on January of 2026, UPS announced it will be retiring its entire fleet of MD-11s as a result of this crash.
Other large companies like FedEx have also temporarily grounded their MD-11 fleets as a precaution.
Today, several families affected have opened up lawsuits against UPS.
There are also several GoFundMe links for those affected, so many that GoFundMe has collected available links into a single URL, available in the description below.
Ultimately, all three flight crew were killed along with another 12 victims on the ground.
22 more were injured.
